changelog: - **A Converter fed through a Gate or another Converter now runs at one fraction with the routers that feed it, and a model whose paths split and meet again is refused before it runs.** Until now a Gate delivered its full share to a Converter before the Converter had decided how much of its recipe it could run, so a Converter with one input from a Gate and another from a short Pool received more than it could use and the difference vanished. Now the Gates and Converters that are joined by connections are planned together, before anything moves: one run fraction for the group, every connection in it moves exactly its share, and the group claims its Pool inputs at the turn of its first router. Because of that claim, a Gate that reads the same Pool and comes between the group's first router and its Converter in the running order now sees the Pool net of the group's claim; a Gate ordered before the group is unaffected. A Converter whose connection from a Gate delivers nothing this step no longer runs on its other inputs alone. One shape has no plan: resources that split at one Gate and meet again at a later Gate or Converter. Such a model is now refused before Play, Step or Monte Carlo start, in every model version, including when the two paths happen to agree: the run bar says so with a Show button, each member of the shape carries the warning outline, and the Inspector says what to change (remove one of the paths, or put a Pool on one of them, which then moves one step later). Editing, saving and sharing are unchanged. A Gate that takes resources from more than one place and passes them to a Converter is not covered yet: it keeps the previous behaviour, and when an amount is lost the run strip now says how much. A saved Monte Carlo distribution computed before this change opens marked as from an earlier version of the engine until you run it again. None of the bundled examples changes.
